value.zh: 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼
value.en: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi
value.literal: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

value.zh: 蕤、臺卿，並有學業。
value.en: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.
value.literal: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.

value.zh: 臺卿文筆尤工，見稱當世。
value.en: Taiqing's brush was especially fine, and his own age praised him.
value.literal: Taiqing's literary brush was especially skilled and he was praised in his age.

value.zh: 蕤字子美，武平中大理少卿，兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。
value.en: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the court of judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and headed the mission to Chen.
value.literal: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the Court of Judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and chief of the mission to Chen.

value.zh: 末年，吏部郎中。
value.en: In his later years he was a langzhong in the ministry of personnel.
value.literal: In his later years he was a langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 隋開皇中，終於開州刺史。
value.en: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.
value.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.

value.zh: 臺卿字少山，歷中書、黃門侍郎，兼大著作、修國史。
value.en: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in turn as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.
value.literal: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in succession as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.

value.zh: 武平末，國子祭酒，領尚書左丞。
value.en: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the imperial university and concurrently left vice director in the masters of writing.
value.literal: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the Imperial University and concurrently held the post of left vice director in the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 周武帝平齊，命尚書左僕射陽休之以下知名朝士十八人隨駕入關，蕤兄弟並不預此名。
value.en: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, left vice director of the masters of writing, downward to follow the train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not on the list.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, downward to follow the imperial train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not among those named.

value.zh: 臺卿後雖被徵，為其聾疾放歸。
value.en: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.
value.literal: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.

value.zh: 隋開皇中，徵為著作郎，歲餘以年老致事，詔許之。
value.en: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the masters of writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired, and an edict allowed it.
value.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the Masters of Writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired from office, and an edict permitted it.

value.zh: 特優其禮，終身給祿，未幾而終。
value.en: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.
value.literal: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.

value.zh: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式
value.en: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, and Jiang Shi
value.literal: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi

value.zh: 臣聞為國之道，其要有五：一曰文德，二曰武功，三曰法度，四曰防固，五曰刑賞。
value.en: I have heard that governing a state rests on five essentials: civil virtue, martial prowess, law and regulation, frontier defense, and the balance of punishment and reward.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that the Way of governing a state has five essentials: first, civil virtue; second, martial achievement; third, laws and standards; fourth, defense and fortification; fifth, punishments and rewards.

value.zh: 故遠人不服，則修文德以來之；
value.en: When distant peoples refuse submission, cultivate civil virtue to win them over;
value.literal: Thus when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in;

value.zh: 荒狡放命，則播武功以威之；
value.en: when savage and defiant enemies run riot, display martial might to overawe them;
value.literal: when wild and cunning men defy orders, deploy martial achievement to awe them;

value.zh: 人未知戰，則制法度以齊之；
value.en: when the people are untrained for war, establish laws and standards to discipline them;
value.literal: when men do not yet know warfare, establish laws and standards to bring them into order;

value.zh: 暴敵輕侵，則設防固以禦之；
value.en: when violent foes raid with impunity, build defenses to hold them off;
value.literal: when violent enemies lightly invade, set up defenses and fortifications to repel them;

value.zh: 臨事制勝，則明賞罰以勸之。
value.en: when victory must be seized in the field, make rewards and punishments clear to spur men on.
value.literal: when facing affairs and securing victory, clarify rewards and punishments to encourage them.

value.zh: 用能辟國甯方，征伐四克。
value.en: By such means a state may expand its borders, secure the realm, and prevail in every campaign.
value.literal: By these means one can open the state and bring the realm to peace, and campaigns and punitive expeditions succeed on all sides.

value.zh: 北狄悍愚，同於禽獸，所長者野戰，所短者攻城。
value.en: The northern barbarians are brutal and simple, little better than animals; they excel at open battle but are weak at siege warfare.
value.literal: The northern Di are fierce and stupid, like birds and beasts; what they excel at is fighting in the wild, what they are poor at is besieging cities.

value.zh: 若以狄之所短，奪其所長，則雖眾不能成患，雖來不能內逼。
value.en: If we exploit their weaknesses to neutralize their strengths, then even in great numbers they cannot threaten us, and even when they come they cannot press deep into our territory.
value.literal: If one uses what the Di are poor at to overcome what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot press inward.

value.zh: 又狄散居野澤，隨逐水草，戰則與室家並至，奔則與畜牧俱逃。
value.en: Moreover they live scattered across marshes and wild country, moving with the pasturage; when they fight they bring their families with them, and when they flee they drive off their herds as well.
value.literal: Moreover the Di live scattered in marshes and wilds, following after water and grass; when they fight they arrive together with their households, when they flee they escape together with their herds.

value.zh: 是以古人伐北方，攘其侵掠而已。
value.en: That is why the ancients, when they campaigned northward, contented themselves with repelling raids and incursions.
value.literal: Therefore the ancients in campaigning against the north merely drove off their raids and invasions.

value.zh: 歷代為邊患者，良以倏忽無常故也。
value.en: Dynasty after dynasty suffered on the frontier chiefly because these enemies struck suddenly and without warning.
value.literal: The reason successive dynasties suffered frontier troubles was truly because the barbarians were sudden and unpredictable.

value.zh: 六鎮勢分，倍眾不鬥，互相圍逼，難以制之。
value.en: The six frontier garrisons are scattered; even at double strength they hesitate to give battle, and when they hem one another in they become difficult to command.
value.literal: The six garrisons are divided in strength; though twice the enemy in number they do not fight, and when they surround and press one another they are hard to control.

value.zh: 昔周命南仲，城彼朔方，趙靈、秦始，長城是築；
value.en: Long ago Zhou commissioned Nanzhong to fortify the northern frontier; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin raised the Long Wall;
value.literal: Formerly Zhou appointed Nanzhong and walled that northern region; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;

value.zh: 漢之孝武，踵其前事。
value.en: and Emperor Wu of Han followed their example.
value.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han followed their earlier deeds.

value.zh: 此四代之君，皆帝王之雄傑，所以同此役者，非智術之不長，兵眾之不足，乃防狄之要事，理宜然也。
value.en: These four rulers were all formidable sovereigns. They undertook the same labor not from lack of strategy or troops, but because guarding against the northern barbarians was essential—and rightly so.
value.literal: These rulers of four dynasties were all heroic emperors and kings; the reason they all undertook this task was not that their wisdom and arts were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter and reason demanded it.

value.zh: 韓襃 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 梁昕 皇甫璠 辛慶之 王子直 杜杲 呂思禮 徐招 檀翥 孟信 宗懍 劉璠 柳遐
value.en: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, and Liu Xia
value.literal: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, Liu Xia

value.zh: 先是，齊寇數入，人廢耕桑，前後刺史，莫能防扞。
value.en: Northern Qi raiders had repeatedly invaded the region, driving the people from their fields; none of Bao's predecessors had been able to stop them.
value.literal: Before this, Qi raiders had repeatedly entered; the people abandoned farming and sericulture; successive governors could not defend against them.

value.zh: 褒至，適會寇來，乃不下屬縣。
value.en: Shortly after Bao took office, raiders struck again—but he did not warn the subordinate counties.
value.literal: When Bao arrived, it happened that raiders came; he did not alert the subordinate counties.

value.zh: 人既不備，以故多被抄掠。
value.en: Caught unprepared, many were robbed.
value.literal: Since the people were unprepared, for this reason many were plundered.

value.zh: 齊人喜於不覺，以為州先未集兵，今還必不能追躡，由是益懈，不為營壘。
value.en: The Qi troops, pleased that no alarm had been raised, assumed the province had no forces ready and that no pursuit would follow. They grew careless and made no fortified camp.
value.literal: The Qi men were pleased at not being detected; they thought the province had not yet gathered troops before, and on returning now surely could not pursue—thereby they grew more slack and did not build camps.

value.zh: 褒已先勒精銳，伏北山中，分據險阻，邀其歸路。
value.en: Bao had already positioned his best troops in ambush in the northern mountains, holding the defiles along the raiders' line of retreat.
value.literal: Bao had already beforehand mustered elite troops, hidden them in the northern mountains, divided and held the dangerous passes, and blocked their return route.

value.zh: 乘其眾怠，縱伏擊之，盡獲其眾。
value.en: When the enemy relaxed their guard, he sprang the ambush and captured the entire raiding party.
value.literal: Taking advantage of their troops' slackness, he released the ambush and struck them, capturing their entire force.

value.zh: 故事，獲生口者，並送京師，褒因是奏曰：「所獲賊眾，不足為多，俘而辱之，但益其忿耳。
value.en: By custom all captives were sent to the capital. Bao memorialized the throne: "These prisoners are too few to matter; holding and humiliating them will only deepen their hatred.
value.literal: By precedent, captives taken alive were all sent to the capital; Bao therefore memorialized: "The bandit force captured is not large enough to matter; to hold them captive and humiliate them only increases their rage.

value.zh: 請一切放還，以德報怨。」
value.en: I beg that they all be released, so that we may repay enmity with kindness."
value.literal: I ask that they all be released and that enmity be answered with virtue."

value.zh: 有詔許焉。
value.en: The emperor approved his request.
value.literal: An edict approved this.

value.zh: 自此抄兵頗息，遷河州總管，仍轉鳳州刺史。
value.en: Raids largely ceased after this. He was appointed commander of He Province and later transferred to governor of Feng.
value.literal: From this raiding troops largely ceased; he was transferred to commander of He Province, then turned to governor of Feng Province.

value.zh: 尋以年老請致事，詔許之。
value.en: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of age, and the emperor granted his request.
value.literal: Soon, on account of age, he requested retirement; an edict granted it.

value.zh: 天和五年，拜少保。
value.en: In the fifth year of the Tianhe era he was appointed junior mentor to the crown prince.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe he was appointed junior mentor.

value.zh: 褒曆事三帝，以忠厚見知。
value.en: Bao served three emperors and was esteemed for his loyalty and integrity.
value.literal: Bao served through three emperors and was known for loyalty and honesty.

value.zh: 武帝深相敬重，常以師道處之，每入朝見，必有詔令坐，然始論政事。
value.en: Emperor Wu held him in the highest regard and always treated him as a teacher. Whenever Bao came to court, the emperor would order him seated before any business was discussed.
value.literal: Emperor Wu deeply respected him, constantly treating him with the ceremony due a teacher; each time he entered court for audience there was always an edict ordering him to be seated before political matters were discussed.

value.zh: 卒，贈涇、岐、燕三州刺史，諡曰貞。
value.en: When he died, he was posthumously honored with the titles of governor of Jing, Qi, and Yan provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).
value.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the three provincial governorships of Jing, Qi, and Yan; his posthumous name was Zhen.

value.zh: 保定二年，為小吏部。
value.en: In the second year of Baoding (562), he was made junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he served as junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 時益州殷阜，軍國所資，經途艱險，每苦劫盜。
value.en: Yizhou was then rich and fertile—the source of supplies for army and state—but the transport routes were treacherous and brigands were a constant scourge.
value.literal: At that time Yizhou was prosperous and fertile, providing resources for army and state; the routes were perilous, and banditry was a constant affliction.

value.zh: 詔昂使于益、梁，軍人之務皆委決焉。
value.en: The emperor ordered Ang to Yi and Liang provinces; all military matters there were placed entirely in his hands.
value.literal: An edict ordered Ang to go as envoy to Yi and Liang; all military affairs were entrusted to his judgment.

value.zh: 昂撫導荒梗，頗得寧靜。
value.en: Ang soothed and guided the wild borderlands until a measure of peace was restored.
value.literal: Ang pacified and guided the rugged frontier regions, achieving considerable tranquility.

value.zh: 天和初，陸騰討信州蠻，詔昂便於通、渠等州運糧饋之。
value.en: Early in the Tianhe era (566), when Lu Teng marched against the Xinxhou tribes, the court ordered Ang to haul grain from Tong, Qu, and neighboring provinces to feed the campaign.
value.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, Lu Teng campaigned against the Man of Xinxhou; an edict ordered Ang to transport grain from Tong, Qu, and other provinces to supply him.

value.zh: 時臨、信、楚、合等諸州人庶多從逆，昂諭以禍福，赴者如歸。
value.en: Many people in Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces had joined the rebels, but when Ang reasoned with them about reward and ruin, they flocked to him as gladly as men returning home.
value.literal: At that time the common people of Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces largely followed the rebels. Ang instructed them regarding fortune and disaster, and those who came to him did so as if returning home.

value.zh: 乃令老弱負糧，壯夫拒戰，莫有怨者。
value.en: He put the old and weak to carrying grain and the able-bodied men to fighting—and not one man murmured against it.
value.literal: He then ordered the old and weak to carry grain and the strong men to resist in battle; none complained.

value.zh: 使還，屬巴州萬榮郡人反叛，圍郡城，昂於是遂募通、開二州，得三千人，倍道兼行，出其不意。
value.en: On his way back, the people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rose in revolt and besieged the commandery seat. Ang promptly raised three thousand men from Tong and Kai, forced a double-time march, and fell upon the rebels before they expected it.
value.literal: When his mission ended and he was returning, people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rebelled and besieged the commandery city. Ang thereupon recruited from Tong and Kai provinces, obtaining three thousand men, marched at double speed day and night, and struck unexpectedly.

value.zh: 又令其眾皆作中國歌，直趣賊壘。
value.en: He also had his men sing Chinese songs as they marched straight for the rebel stronghold.
value.literal: He also ordered his troops all to sing songs of China and go straight toward the rebel camp.

value.zh: 謂有大軍赴救，望風瓦解。
value.en: Believing a large relief force was at hand, the rebels broke apart at the first sign of them.
value.literal: Thinking a great army was coming to the rescue, the rebels dispersed at the mere sight of them.

value.zh: 朝廷嘉其權以濟事，詔梁州總管、杞國公亮即於軍中賞昂奴婢二十口，繒彩四百匹。
value.en: The court applauded his resourcefulness in bringing the affair to success and ordered Liangzhou's regional commander, Duke Liang of Qi, to reward Ang on the spot with twenty household slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.
value.literal: The court praised his expedient measures for achieving the task; an edict ordered Liang Province regional commander, Duke of Qi State Liang, to reward Ang in camp with twenty slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.

value.zh: 又以昂威信布于宕梁，遂表為渠州刺史。
value.en: Since Ang's authority and credibility now reached throughout Dangliang, the court memorialized him for appointment as governor of Qu Province.
value.literal: Because Ang's prestige and trust had spread through Dangliang, he was memorialized for appointment as governor of Qu Province.

value.zh: 轉通州。
value.en: He was transferred to Tong Province.
value.literal: He was transferred to Tong Province.

value.zh: 推誠布信，甚得夷獠歡心。
value.en: By treating them with open sincerity and steadfast trust, he won the deep loyalty of the tribal peoples.
value.literal: He extended sincerity and spread good faith, greatly winning the hearts of the Yi and Liao peoples.

value.zh: 秩滿還京，首領皆隨昂詣闕朝覲。
value.en: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs accompanied him to court for an imperial audience.
value.literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs all followed Ang to the palace to pay court audience.

value.zh: 以昂化洽夷落，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
value.en: In recognition of his civilizing work among the frontier tribes, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the privilege of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies.
value.literal: Because Ang's transforming influence had reached the barbarian settlements, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Commissioner with the Same Privileges as a Three-in-One Grand Officer.

value.zh: 時晉公護執政，昂稍被護親待，武帝頗銜之。
value.en: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the reins of government, and Ang gradually won Hu's personal favor—a fact that Emperor Wu took rather badly.
value.literal: At that time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Ang came gradually to enjoy Hu's intimate favor, and Emperor Wu harbored considerable resentment.

value.zh: 及誅護，加之捶楚，因此遂卒。
value.en: When Hu was put to death, Ang was beaten and flogged as well and died from it.
value.literal: When Hu was executed, Ang was subjected to beating and torture and thereby died.

value.zh: 祥字休徵。
value.en: Xiang, whose style name was Xiuzheng.
value.literal: Xiang, style name Xiuzheng.

value.zh: 幼聰慧，賓客見者皆號神童。
value.en: From childhood he was clever and bright; every guest who saw him called him a prodigy.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and intelligent; all guests who saw him called him a divine child.

value.zh: 事嫡母以至孝聞。
value.en: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.
value.literal: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.

value.zh: 其伯父黃門郎璆，有名江左，在嶺南，聞而奇之，乃令名祥字休徵。
value.en: His father's elder brother Qiu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of the boy in Lingnan, he marveled and had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.
value.literal: His father's elder brother, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Qiu, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of him in Lingnan, he marveled and therefore had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.

value.zh: 後以字行於世。
value.en: Later he was known in the world by his style name.
value.literal: Later he was known in the world by his style name.

value.zh: 十歲能屬文，十二通《五經》。
value.en: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he had mastered the Five Classics.
value.literal: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he mastered the Five Classics.

value.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯記室參軍。
value.en: Under Liang he served as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.
value.literal: He served Liang as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.

value.zh: 江陵平，隨例入關中。
value.en: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass with the other captives.
value.literal: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass according to precedent.

value.zh: 齊公憲召為記室，府中書記皆令掌之。
value.en: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.
value.literal: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.

value.zh: 封漢安縣子。
value.en: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.
value.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.

value.zh: 憲進爵為王，以休徵為王友。
value.en: When Xian was raised to princely rank, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.
value.literal: When Xian advanced in rank to prince, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.

value.zh: 俄除內史上士。
value.en: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.
value.literal: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.

value.zh: 武帝東征，休徵陪侍帷幄，平齊露布即休徵文也。
value.en: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was written by Xiuzheng.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was Xiuzheng's composition.

value.zh: 累遷車騎大將軍、儀同大將軍。
value.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.

value.zh: 曆長安、萬年二縣令，頗獲時譽。
value.en: He served in succession as magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.
value.literal: He successively served as Magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.

value.zh: 卒於官。
value.en: He died in office.
value.literal: He died in office.

value.zh: 初，璠所選《梁典》始就，未及刊定而卒，臨終謂休徵曰：「能成我志，其在此書乎！」
value.en: The Liang Canon that Fan had compiled was just finished but not yet edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng, "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!
value.literal: At first the Liang Canon that Fan compiled was just finished but had not yet been edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng: "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!

value.zh: 休徵修定繕寫。
value.en: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.
value.literal: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.

value.zh: 勒成一家，行於世。
value.en: He brought it to completion as a work in its own right, and it circulated in his day.
value.literal: He completed it as a work in its own right, and it circulated in the world.

value.zh: 儒林下
value.en: Confucian Scholars, Part Two
value.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.

value.zh: 時外史廨宇屢移，未有定所。
value.en: At that time the outer historians’ offices were repeatedly relocated and had no fixed site.
value.literal: At that time the offices of the outer historians were repeatedly moved and had no fixed site.

value.zh: 季明又上言曰：「外史之職，漢之東觀，帝王所寶，此焉攸在。
value.en: Jiming submitted another memorial: “The office of outer historian corresponds to the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is kept here.
value.literal: Jiming again submitted a memorial, saying, “The office of outer historian is the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is preserved here.

value.zh: 自魏及周，公館不立，臣雖愚瞽，猶知其非。
value.en: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.
value.literal: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.

value.zh: 是以去年十一月中，敢冒奏陳，特降中旨，即遣修營。
value.en: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.
value.literal: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared to memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.

value.zh: 荏苒一周，未知功力。
value.en: A full year has passed and the progress of the work is still unknown.
value.literal: A year has passed and the work accomplished is still unknown.

value.zh: 臣職思其憂，敢不重請。」
value.en: The duties of my office weigh upon my mind; I dare press the request again."
value.literal: My office weighs upon my mind; I dare again to press the request."

value.zh: 帝納焉，於是廨宇方立。
value.en: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.
value.literal: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.

value.zh: 天和二年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
value.en: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
value.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 後以疾卒。
value.en: He later died of illness.
value.literal: Later he died of illness.

value.zh: 高麗 百濟 新羅 勿吉 奚 契丹 室韋 豆莫婁 地豆幹 烏洛侯 流求 倭
value.en: Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Wuji, Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didougan, Wuluohou, Liuqiu, and Japan
value.literal: Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Wuji, Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didougan, Wuluohou, Liuqiu, Japan

value.zh: 成死，子湯立。
value.en: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded him.
value.literal: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded.

value.zh: 乾明元年，齊廢帝以湯爲使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。
value.en: In the first year of Qianming the Deposed Emperor of Qi invested Tang as holder of the staff of authority, colonel of the Eastern Yi, duke of Liaodong commandery, and king of Goguryeo.
value.literal: In the first year of Qianming, the Deposed Emperor of Qi made Tang Holder of the Staff, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

value.zh: 周建德六年，湯遣使至周，武帝以湯爲上開府儀同大將軍、遼東郡公、遼東王。
value.en: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou, and Emperor Wu of Zhou invested him as Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Liaodong.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou; Emperor Wu of Zhou made Tang Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Liaodong.

value.zh: 隋文帝受禪，湯遣使詣闕，進授大將軍，改封高麗王。
value.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Tang sent envoys to court, was promoted to Grand General, and was re-invested as King of Goguryeo.
value.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Tang sent envoys to the court; he was promoted to Grand General and re-invested as King of Goguryeo.

value.zh: 自是，歲遣使朝貢不絕。
value.en: From then on tribute envoys came every year without fail.
value.literal: From this onward, tribute envoys were sent every year without interruption.

value.zh: 王昌一名郎，趙國邯鄲人也。
value.en: Wang Chang, who also went by the name Wang Lang, came from Handan in Zhao.
value.literal: Wang Chang, another name Lang, was a man of Handan in the state of Zhao.

value.zh: 素為卜相工，明星曆，常以為河北有天子氣。
value.en: He made his living reading omens and faces, knew the stars and the calendar, and had long been convinced that the region north of the river bore the portents of an emperor.
value.literal: He had long worked as a diviner and physiognomist, understood the stars and calendars, and constantly believed that north of the Yellow River there was the aura of a Son of Heaven.

value.zh: 時趙繆王子林，景帝七代孫也，好奇數，任俠於趙、魏間，多通豪猾，而郎與之親善。
value.en: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.
value.literal: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.

value.zh: 初，王莽篡位，長安中或自稱成帝子子輿者，莽殺之。
value.en: After Wang Mang usurped the throne, a man in Chang’an had claimed to be Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng; Mang had him executed.
value.literal: Earlier, when Wang Mang seized the throne, someone in Chang’an who called himself Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng, was killed by Mang.

value.zh: 郎緣是詐稱真子輿，云『母故成帝謳者，嘗下殿卒僵，須臾有黃氣從上下，半日乃解，遂妊身就館。
value.en: Wang Lang therefore passed himself off as the genuine Liu Ziyu, claiming: "My mother was once a palace singer to Emperor Cheng. She once came down from the hall and suddenly collapsed; after a little while yellow vapor flowed down from above, and only after half a day did she recover. She then conceived and was sent to the birth house.
value.literal: Lang on this account falsely called himself the true Ziyu, saying: ‘My mother had been a singer for Emperor Cheng; once when descending the hall she suddenly collapsed stiff; in a moment yellow vapour came from above and below; only after half a day did she recover, and then she was pregnant and went to the lying-in quarters.

value.zh: 趙後欲害之，偽易他人子，以故得全。
value.en: Empress Zhao tried to destroy me, but another person's child was substituted as a deception, and so I was preserved.
value.literal: Empress Zhao wished to harm him; she falsely exchanged another person’s child; by this means he was preserved whole.

value.zh: 子輿年十二，識命者郎中李曼卿，與俱至蜀；
value.en: At twelve, Ziyu met the physiognomist and court gentleman Li Manqing and traveled with him into Shu;
value.literal: When Ziyu was twelve, he met the fate-reader Gentleman-of-the-Palace Li Manqing and together with him went to Shu.

value.zh: 十七，到丹陽；
value.en: at seventeen, he reached Danyang;
value.literal: At seventeen, he arrived at Danyang.

value.zh: 二十，還長安；
value.en: at twenty, he returned to Chang'an;
value.literal: At twenty, he returned to Chang’an.

value.zh: 展轉中山，來往燕、趙，以須天時』。
value.en: then he drifted through Zhongshan and between Yan and Zhao, waiting for Heaven's time."
value.literal: He shifted to Zhongshan, coming and going between Yan and Zhao, in order to await the heavenly season.’

value.zh: 林等愈動疑惑，乃與趙國大豪李育、張參等通謀，規共立郎。
value.en: The story unsettled Liu Lin and his circle; they conspired with Zhao notables Li Yu and Zhang Can to set Wang Lang on the throne.
value.literal: Lin and the others were increasingly moved to doubt, and then with great magnates of Zhao such as Li Yu and Zhang Can secretly plotted, planning together to establish Lang.

value.zh: 會人間傳赤眉將度河，林等因此宣言赤眉當立劉子輿以觀眾心，百姓多信之。
value.en: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.
value.literal: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.

value.zh: 盧芳字君期，安定三水人也，居左谷中。
value.en: Lu Fang, styled Junqi, was from Sanshui in Anding and lived in the Zuogu valley.
value.literal: Lu Fang, styled Junqi, was from Sanshui in Anding and lived in the Zuogu valley.

value.zh: 王莽時，天下咸思漢德，芳由是詐自稱武帝曾孫劉文伯。
value.en: While Wang Mang held the realm, men everywhere missed the virtue of Han; Lu Fang therefore passed himself off as Liu Wenbo, a great-grandson of Emperor Wu.
value.literal: In Wang Mang's time, all under heaven longed for Han virtue; Fang on this account falsely styled himself Emperor Wu's great-grandson Liu Wenbo.

value.zh: 曾祖母匈奴谷蠡渾邪王之姊為武帝皇后，生三子。
value.en: His alleged great-grandmother was the sister of the Xiongnu prince Hunye of the Guili rank, who became Emperor Wu’s empress and bore three sons.
value.literal: His great-grandmother was the Xiongnu Guili Hunye King's elder sister who became Emperor Wu's empress; she bore three sons.

value.zh: 遭江充之亂，太子誅，皇后坐死，中子次卿亡之長陵，小子回卿逃於左谷。
value.en: When Jiang Chong’s intrigue struck down the heir, the empress died with him; the middle son, Ciqing, fled to Changling and the youngest, Huiqing, to the Zuogu valley.
value.literal: They suffered Jiang Chong's turmoil; the heir was executed; the empress died by implication; the middle son Ciqing fled to Changling; the youngest son Huiqing fled to Zuogu.

value.zh: 霍將軍立次卿，迎回卿。
value.en: General Huo Guang set up Ciqing and sent for Huiqing.
value.literal: General Huo established Ciqing, welcomed Huiqing.

value.zh: 回卿不出，因居左谷，生子孫卿，孫卿生文伯。
value.en: Huiqing would not emerge and stayed on in Zuogu; his line ran Sunqing and then Wenbo.
value.literal: Huiqing did not come out, therefore dwelt in Zuogu, bore a son Sunqing; Sunqing bore Wenbo.

value.zh: 常以是言誑惑安定間。
value.en: Lu Fang peddled this tale through Anding for years.
value.literal: He constantly used these words to deceive and confuse within Anding.

value.zh: 王莽末，乃與三水屬國羌胡起兵。
value.en: At the close of Wang Mang’s reign he rose with the Qiang and Hu of the Sanshui dependent state.
value.literal: At Wang Mang's end, then together with the dependent state's Qiang and Hu of Sanshui he raised troops.

value.zh: 更始至長安，征芳為騎都尉，使鎮撫安定以西。
value.en: When the Gengshi court entered Chang’an it summoned Lu Fang as cavalry commandant and sent him to pacify the country west of Anding.
value.literal: When Gengshi reached Chang'an, he summoned Fang as cavalry commandant, ordered him to pacify and comfort west of Anding.

value.zh: 《續漢志》曰三水縣有左右谷，故城在今涇州安定縣南。
value.en: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.
value.literal: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.

value.zh: 長伯，豐字也。
value.en: Changbo was Feng’s style name.
value.literal: Changbo was Feng’s style name.

value.zh: 豐，平帝時為少府，王莽篡位時為更始將軍。
value.en: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.
value.literal: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.

value.zh: 好奇數，術數。
value.en: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.
value.literal: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.

value.zh: 《王莽傳》曰，時男子武仲自稱劉子輿。
value.en: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.
value.literal: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.

value.zh: 趙飛燕也。
value.en: This was Zhao Feiyan.
value.literal: This was Zhao Feiyan.

value.zh: 《東觀記》曰：「宮婢生子，正與同時，即易之」也。
value.en: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”
value.literal: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”

value.zh: 識命謂知天命也。
value.en: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.
value.literal: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.

value.zh: 須，待也。
value.en: Xu means “to wait.”
value.literal: Xu means “to wait.”

value.zh: 耿弇字伯昭，扶風茂陵人也。
value.en: Geng Yan, courtesy name Bozhao, was a native of Maoling in Fufeng commandery.
value.literal: Geng Yan, styled Bozhao, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.

value.zh: 其先武帝時以吏二千石自巨鹿徙焉。
value.en: His forebears had held a two-thousand-dan post under Emperor Wu and relocated from Julu to Maoling.
value.literal: His ancestors, in the time of Emperor Wu, as officials at the rank of two thousand shi, moved from Julu to there.

value.zh: 父況，字俠遊，以明經為郎，與王莽從弟伋共學《老子》於安丘先生，後為朔調連率。
value.en: His father Geng Kuang, courtesy name Xiayou, entered court as a gentleman-attendant on the strength of his classical learning; with Wang Mang's cousin Wang Ji he studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, and was later appointed chain commandant of the Shuodiao circuit.
value.literal: His father Kuang, styled Xiayou, through understanding the classics became a gentleman-attendant, and with Wang Mang's cousin Ji together studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, afterward became chain commandant of Shuodiao.

value.zh: 弇少好學，習父業。
value.en: From boyhood Geng Yan loved learning and followed his father's scholarly path.
value.literal: Yan in youth loved study, practiced his father's occupation.

value.zh: 常見郡尉試騎士，建旗鼓，肄馳射，由是好將帥之事。
value.en: He often watched the commandery commandant drill mounted archers—drums and banners raised, bows shot at full gallop—and so grew fond of the business of command.
value.literal: He often saw the commandery commandant test mounted knights, set up drums and banners, drill mounted archery, thereby came to love generals' and commanders' affairs.

value.zh: 東海恭王彊
value.en: King Gong of the East Sea, Liu Qiang
value.literal: King Gong of East Sea, Qiang.

value.zh: 並遺宛馬一匹，血從前髆上小孔中出。
value.en: With it goes a Ferghana horse whose blood beads from a pore on the shoulder.
value.literal: Together leave Wan horse one piece—blood from front shoulder blade upper small hole emerges.

value.zh: 常聞武帝歌天馬，沾赤汗，今親見其然也。
value.en: I grew up on the songs of Emperor Wu's sweating steeds—now I have seen one.
value.literal: Constantly heard Martial Emperor sing heaven horse—stained red sweat—now personally see it thus.

value.zh: 頃反虜尚屯，將帥在外，憂念遑遑，未有閒寧。
value.en: [68] Rebels still hold the field and our generals are abroad—I have no peace of mind.
value.literal: [68] Recently rebel captives still camp—generals outside—worry thought restless—have not yet idle peace.

value.zh: 願王寶精神，加供養。
value.en: [69] Guard your health and take care of yourself.
value.literal: [69] Wish king treasure spirit—add nourishing.

value.zh: 苦言至戒，望之如渴。」
value.en: I thirst for your blunt counsel."
value.literal: Bitter words utmost warning—long for them like thirst."

value.zh: 楊終字子山，蜀郡成都人也。
value.en: Yang Zhong, styled Zishan, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
value.literal: Yang Zhong, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 年十三，為郡小吏，太守奇其才，遣詣京師受業，習春秋。
value.en: When he was thirteen he served as a junior clerk in the commandery. The grand administrator, struck by his ability, sent him to the capital for schooling, and there he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
value.literal: At age thirteen he became a petty clerk in the commandery; the grand administrator marveled at his talent and sent him to the capital to study, where he learned the Chunqiu.

value.zh: [一]顯宗時，征詣蘭台，拜校書郎。
value.en: Under Emperor Ming he was called to the Orchid Terrace and given the post of collating secretary [1].
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming [note 1], he was summoned to the Orchid Terrace and appointed collator.

value.zh: 初，酺之為大匠，上言：「孝文皇帝始置一經博士，[一]武帝大合天下之書，[二] 而孝宣論六經於石渠，學者滋盛，弟子萬數。
value.en: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.
value.literal: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.

value.zh: [三]光武初興，愍其荒廢，起太學博士捨、內外講堂，諸生橫巷，為海內所集。
value.en: [3] Emperor Guangwu, grieving the ruin of learning, had rebuilt the Grand Academy with dormitories, inner and outer lecture halls, and student quarters that drew scholars from everywhere.
value.literal: [3] When Guangwu first rose, pitying their ruin and waste, he raised the Grand Academy, erudite lodgings, inner and outer lecture halls, and lanes of students—it became the gathering place of the realm.

value.zh: 明帝時辟雍始成，欲毀太學，太尉趙憙以為太學、辟雍皆宜兼存，故並傳至今。
value.en: When Emperor Ming finished the circular moat school, some wanted the Grand Academy torn down; Grand Commandant Zhao Xi argued that both institutions should survive, and both stand today.
value.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, when the Biyong was first completed, they wished to destroy the Grand Academy. Grand Commandant Zhao Xi held that the Grand Academy and the Biyong should both be kept, and therefore both have been transmitted to the present.

value.zh: 而頃者頹廢，至為園采芻牧之處。
value.en: Lately the grounds had fallen into disuse as vegetable patches, hayfields, and sheep walks.
value.literal: But recently it has decayed and wasted until it became a place for garden plots, gathering fodder, and herding.

value.zh: 宜更修繕，誘進後學。」
value.en: Zhai Pu urged a fresh restoration to attract the next generation of learners."
value.literal: It is fitting to repair and build anew and entice later students.'

value.zh: 帝從之。
value.en: The emperor accepted the advice.
value.literal: The emperor followed it.'"

value.zh: 酺免後，遂起太學，更開拓房室，學者為酺立碑銘於學雲。
value.en: After his disgrace the Grand Academy was rebuilt and expanded; students are said to have raised a stele in his honor on the campus.
value.literal: After Pu was dismissed, thereupon they raised the Grand Academy, again opened and expanded rooms, and scholars set up a stele inscription for Pu at the academy, it is said.

value.zh: 注[一]武帝建元五年始置五經博士，文帝之時未遑庠序之事，酺之此言，不知何據。
value.en: Commentary [1]: Emperor Wu first established Erudites for the Five Classics in the fifth year of Jianyuan. In Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for affairs of schools and academies, so it is unclear what authority Zhai Pu had for this statement.
value.literal: Note [1] In Emperor Wu's Jianyuan 5 the five-classics erudites were first established; in Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for school matters—what Pu's statement relies on is unknown.

value.zh: 注[二]武帝詔曰：「其令禮官勸學，舉遺興禮。」
value.en: Commentary [2]: "Emperor Wu had ordered the ritual bureau to revive neglected learning and rites."
value.literal: Note [2] Emperor Wu's edict said: 'Let the ritual officials encourage learning and raise the lost and promote ritual.'

value.zh: 舉遺謂搜求遺逸，是合天下之書也。
value.en: Raising the lost meant recovering lost texts, that is, the empire-wide book hunt.
value.literal: Raise the lost' means to search out the scattered and hidden—this is gathering the books of All under Heaven.'

value.zh: 馬融字季長，扶風茂陵人也，[一]將作大匠嚴之子。
value.en: Ma Rong, styled Jizhang, came from Maoling in Fufeng. He was the son of Yan, who served as Grand Architect of Works.
value.literal: Ma Rong, courtesy name Jizhang, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng; [1] he was the son of Yan, the Grand Architect.

value.zh: [二]為人美辭貌，有俊才。
value.en: He was gifted in both speech and looks, and carried uncommon intellectual brilliance.
value.literal: [2] In person he was handsome in speech and bearing, and possessed outstanding talent.

value.zh: 注[一二]方猶並也。
value.en: Fang marks paired hulls.
value.literal: Note [12] Fang means side by side.

value.zh: 余皇，吳之船名也。
value.en: Yuhuang was the great Wu dreadnought.
value.literal: Yuhuang is Wu’s ship name.

value.zh: 見左傳。
value.en: See Zuo’s battle of Huangchi.
value.literal: See the Zuo Zhuan.

value.zh: 舼，小舟也，音渠恭反。
value.en: Qiong skiffs use fanqie qu-gong.
value.literal: Qiong is a small boat; pronunciation qu-gong fan.

value.zh: 淮南子曰：「越舼、蜀艇，不能無水而浮。」
value.en: The Huainanzi says: "Yue qiong and Shu boats cannot float without water."
value.literal: The Huainanzi says: "Yue qiong and Shu boats cannot float without water."

value.zh: 帆音凡。
value.en: Fan as in ‘sail.’
value.literal: Fan is pronounced fan.

value.zh: 幬，帳也，音直由反。
value.en: Chou is awning—fanqie zhi-you.
value.literal: Chou is canopy; pronunciation zhi-you fan.

value.zh: 颸，疾風也，音楚疑也。
value.en: Si names slick breezes.
value.literal: Si is swift wind; pronunciation chu-yi.

value.zh: 武帝秋風詞曰：「蕭鼓鳴兮發棹歌。」
value.en: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."
value.literal: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."

value.zh: 劉向列女傳曰：「津更之女，中流奏河激之歌。」
value.en: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."
value.literal: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."

value.zh: 韓詩外傳曰：「瓠巴鼓琴，淫魚出聽。」
value.en: The Han shi waizhuan says: "When Hu Ba strummed his qin, leaping fish came out to listen."
value.literal: The Han shi waizhuan says: "When Hu Ba strummed his qin, leaping fish came out to listen."

value.zh: 淮南子曰：「上有叢蓍，下有伏龜。」
value.en: The Huainanzi says: "Where clusters of yarrow grow above, turtles lie below."
value.literal: The Huainanzi says: "Where clusters of yarrow grow above, turtles lie below."

value.zh: 論語曰：「臧文仲居蔡。」
value.en: The Analects says: "Zang Wenzhong housed the Cai tortoise."
value.literal: The Analects says: "Zang Wenzhong housed the Cai tortoise."

value.zh: 注云：「龜出蔡地，故以為名也。」
value.en: Commentary says: "The tortoise came from Cai lands—hence the name."
value.literal: Commentary says: "The tortoise came from Cai lands—hence the name."

value.zh: 湘靈，舜妃，溺於湘水，為湘夫人也。
value.en: Lady Xiang guards the Xiang shallows.
value.literal: Xiang Ling is Shun’s consort—she drowned in the Xiang and became Lady Xiang.

value.zh: 見楚詞。
value.en: See the Songs of Chu.
value.literal: See the Chu ci.

value.zh: 漢女，漢水之神*[女]*。
value.en: Han Maiden personifies the Han.
value.literal: Han Maiden is the goddess of the Han River.

value.zh: 詩云：「漢有游女。」
value.en: The Canon sings ‘Han girls at play.’
value.literal: The poem says: "On the Han roam touring girls."

value.zh: 左雄字伯豪，南*
value.en: Zuo Xiong, whose courtesy name was Bohao, came from Nanyang commandery
value.literal: Zuo Xiong, courtesy name Bohao, was a native of Nanyang

value.en: (the commandery name)
value.literal: (commandery)

value.zh: **[陽]*涅陽人也。
value.en: specifically of Nieyang.
value.literal: [Yang]—of Nieyang.

value.zh: 安帝時，舉孝廉，稍遷冀州刺史。
value.en: During the reign of Emperor An, he was nominated as filial and incorrupt and rose step by step to the governorship of Ji Province.
value.literal: Under Emperor An, he was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and was gradually promoted to Governor of Ji Province.

value.zh: 州部多豪族，好請托，雄常閉門不與交通。
value.en: The region was full of powerful families who habitually pulled strings; Zuo Xiong routinely kept his gate closed and refused such traffic.
value.literal: The province abounded in powerful clans who loved to seek favors through connections; Xiong often shut his doors and had no dealings with them.

value.zh: 奏案貪猾二千石，無所回忌。
value.en: He impeached and prosecuted venal and evasive prefects and commandery governors, showing neither hesitation nor favor.
value.literal: He memorialized to investigate corrupt and slippery two-thousand-dan officials, without any turning back or scruple.

value.zh: 注[二]萬歲亭在今洛州故嵩陽縣西北。
value.en: Note [2]: Wansui Post stood northwest of old Songyang.
value.literal: Note [2] Wansui Pavilion is northwest of the old Songyang county in modern Luo prefecture.

value.zh: 武帝元封元年，幸緱氏，登太室，聞山上呼萬歲聲者三，因以名焉。
value.en: In the first year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Wu of Han, the emperor visited Goushi, climbed Taishi, and heard cries of "long life" three times from the mountain; he therefore named the place Wansui.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Wu of Han, the emperor visited Goushi, climbed Taishi, and heard cries of "long life" three times from the mountain; he therefore named the place Wansui.

value.zh: 論曰：古者諸侯歲貢士，進賢受上賞，非賢貶爵土。
value.en: The historian remarks: feudal lords once presented talent yearly; recommending worthies won reward, sending dross cost rank.
value.literal: The essay says: In antiquity the feudal lords yearly presented scholars; advancing the worthy received upper reward, presenting the unworthy demoted rank and territory.

value.zh: 升之司馬，辯論其才，論定然後官之，任官然後祿之。
value.en: Candidates went to the minister of war for debate, then office, then salary.
value.literal: They raised them to the Minister of War, debated their talents, fixed the evaluation and then gave them office, gave them office and then salary.

value.zh: [一]故王者得其人，進仕勸其行，經邦弘務，所由久矣。
value.en: [1] Thus wise kings matched men to posts and built lasting rule.
value.literal: [1] Therefore when the king obtained the right men, promotion encouraged their conduct; ordering the state and magnifying tasks—this is the source of long endurance.

value.zh: 漢初詔舉賢良、方正，州郡察孝廉、秀才，斯亦貢士之方也。
value.en: Han edicts called for worthies; provinces nominated filial and cultivated talents—the same principle.
value.literal: At the beginning of Han edicts summoned worthy, good, and upright men; provinces and commanderies inspected filial and incorrupt and cultivated talents—this too was the method of presenting scholars.

value.zh: 中興以後，復增敦樸、有道、賢能、直言、獨行、高節、質直、清白、敦厚之屬。
value.en: After Guangwu came further categories—honest, reclusive, outspoken, and the like.
value.literal: After the restoration, again were added honest and plain, possessed of the Way, worthy and able, straight-speaking, solitary in conduct, lofty in integrity, plain and straight, pure and white, honest and thick—and such categories.

value.zh: 榮路既廣，觖望難裁，自是竊名偽服，浸以流競。
value.en: Broad paths to honor bred false reputations and fierce rivalry.
value.literal: With honor roads so wide, disappointed hopes were hard to restrain; from this stealing names and false garb gradually flowed into reckless competition.

value.zh: 權門貴仕，請謁繁興。
value.en: Great houses and high posts traded favors openly.
value.literal: Powerful gates and noble offices—seeking favor and visiting flourished.

value.zh: 自左雄任事，限年試才，雖頗有不密，固亦因識時宜。
value.en: Zuo Xiong's age limits and exams, though imperfect, fit the age.
value.literal: From the time Zuo Xiong held office, limiting years and testing talent—although there were places not tight, it solidly was because he recognized the times' needs.

value.zh: 而黃瓊、胡廣、張衡、崔瑗之徒，泥滯舊方，互相詭駁，循名者屈其短，筭實者挺其□。
value.en: Huang Qiong, Hu Guang, Zhang Heng, and Cui Yuan clung to old rules and crossed purposes—formalists hid faults, realists exposed them.
value.literal: Yet Huang Qiong, Hu Guang, Zhang Heng, Cui Yuan, and such men, stuck in old patterns, mutually made strange refutations; those who followed names bent their shortcomings, those who calculated substance straightened their [lacuna].

value.zh: 故雄在尚書，天下不敢妄選，十餘年閒，稱為得人，斯亦□實之征乎？
value.en: Under Zuo Xiong the capital dared not traffic in office for a decade—proof that substance could be tested.
value.literal: Therefore while Xiong was at the Masters of Writing, the realm under Heaven did not dare recklessly select; within more than ten years he was called to have obtained the right men—is this not a sign of [lacuna] substance?

value.zh: 順帝始以童弱反政，而號令自出，知能任使，故士得用情，天下喁喁仰其風采。
value.en: Emperor Shun, though young, held real power, chose men well, and the empire looked up to him.
value.literal: When Emperor Shun first took the government back from childhood, yet commands issued from himself, knowing how to employ men, therefore scholars could use their sincerity; all under Heaven craned their necks admiring his bearing.

value.zh: 遂乃備玄纁玉帛，以聘南陽樊英，天子降寢殿，設□席，尚書奉引，延問失得。
value.en: He sent black and yellow silks to hire Fan Ying, received him below the imperial couch, and asked what was wrong with the state.
value.literal: Thereupon he prepared dark and light silks and jade and silk to hire Fan Ying of Nanyang; the Son of Heaven descended to the sleeping hall, spread [lacuna] mats, the Master of Writing led the way, and extended inquiry on gains and losses.

value.zh: 急登賢之舉，虛降己之禮，於是處士鄙生，忘其拘儒，[二]拂巾衽褐，以企旌車之招矣。
value.en: Such urgency to find talent and humility toward scholars made hermits dust off caps and wait for the imperial carriage.
value.literal: Urgent in elevating the worthy, humble in lowering himself—in this way recluses and rustic scholars forgot their cramped Confucianism, [2] brushed caps and wore coarse cloth, hoping for the summoning carriage's invitation.

value.zh: 至乃英能承風，俊乂鹹事，若李固、周舉之淵謨弘深，左雄、黃瓊之政事貞固，桓焉、楊厚以儒學進，崔瑗、馬融以文章顯，吳佑、蘇章、種暠、欒巴牧民之良干，龐參、虞詡將帥之宏規，王龔、張皓虛心以推士，張綱、杜喬直道以糾違，郎顗陰陽詳密，張衡機術特妙：東京之士，於茲盛焉。
value.en: Fan Ying answered the call; Li Gu, Zhou Ju, Zuo Xiong, Huang Qiong, Huan Yan, Yang Hou, Cui Yuan, Ma Rong, Wu You, Su Zhang, Chong Hao, Luan Ba, Pang Shen, Yu Xu, Wang Gong, Zhang Hao, Zhang Gang, Du Qiao, Lang Yi, and Zhang Heng—statesmen, generals, and scientists—made the eastern capital bloom.
value.literal: Thus even Ying could catch the wind, and the talented all served—such as the deep and broad counsel of Li Gu and Zhou Ju, the upright administration of Zuo Xiong and Huang Qiong, Huan Yan and Yang Hou advancing by Confucian learning, Cui Yuan and Ma Rong displaying literary brilliance, Wu You, Su Zhang, Chong Hao, and Luan Ba as fine tools for shepherding the people, Pang Shen and Yu Xu as grand models for generals, Wang Gong and Zhang Hao with open mind recommending scholars, Zhang Gang and Du Qiao with straight path correcting violations, Lang Yi detailed in yin-yang, Zhang Heng uniquely subtle in devices and arts: the scholars of eastern capital flourished here.

value.zh: 向使廟堂納其高謀，強*
value.en: Had high policy taken their counsel, and on every contested
value.literal: If the court had accepted their high plans, and on the hard-fought

value.en: (battle)
value.literal: (battle)

value.zh: **[埸]*宣其智力，帷幄容其謇辭，舉厝稟其成式，則武、宣之軌，豈其遠而？
value.en: frontier, generals had matched wit to force, while the inner court heard blunt truth and the throne followed their models—the glory of Emperors Wu and Xuan would lie within reach.
value.literal: [frontier] field commanders had deployed their wit and strength, if the inner tent had welcomed blunt counsel and every decision had followed their proven models—would the age of Wu and Xuan be far away?

value.zh: [三]詩云：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」
value.en: [3] The Odes say, 'Few can finish what they begin.'
value.literal: [3] The Poetry says: "There is none without a beginning; few can keep the end."

value.zh: 可為恨哉！
value.en: A lasting regret!
value.literal: It can be counted a regret!

value.zh: 及孝桓之時，碩德繼興，[四]陳蕃、楊秉處稱賢宰，皇甫、張、段出號名將，王暢、李膺彌縫袞闕，[五]朱穆、劉陶獻替匡時，郭有道□鑒人倫，陳仲弓弘道下邑。
value.en: Under Emperor Huan came Chen Fan, Yang Bing, Huangfu Song, Zhang Huan, Duan Jiong, Wang Chang, Li Ying, Zhu Mu, Liu Tao, Guo Tai, and Chen Shi—statesmen who shored up the throne.
value.literal: By the time of Emperor Huan, great virtue arose in succession, [4] Chen Fan and Yang Bing at court were called worthy chancellors, Huangfu, Zhang, and Duan abroad were famed generals, Wang Chang and Li Ying patched the emperor's robe, [5] Zhu Mu and Liu Tao offered counsel to correct the age, Guo Tai [lacuna] mirrored human relations, Chen Zhong expanded the Way in a lowly county.

value.zh: 其餘宏儒遠智，高心絜行，激揚風流者，不可勝言。
value.en: Other great scholars and pure men are too many to list.
value.literal: The rest—great Confucians and far-seeing men, high in mind and pure in conduct, who stirred the currents—cannot all be told.

value.zh: 而斯道莫振，文武陵隊，在朝者以正議嬰戮，謝事者以黨錮致□。
value.en: Yet the way withered: courtiers died for speaking truth; retirees were caught in faction bans.
value.literal: Yet this way did not flourish; civil and military fell in ranks; those at court met slaughter for upright counsel; those who retired met proscription from faction.

value.zh: 往車雖折，而來軫方遒。
value.en: The front axle snapped, but the rear wheels still thundered.
value.literal: The forward carriage though broken, yet the coming axle-boxes are still strong.

value.zh: [六] 所以傾而未顛，決而未潰，豈非仁人君子心力之為乎？
value.en: [6] The dynasty leaned yet stood, cracked yet held—thanks to humane men who braced it.
value.literal: [6] That therefore it leaned yet did not topple, burst yet did not collapse—is it not the work of the hearts and strength of humane gentlemen?

value.zh: 嗚呼！
value.en: What a pity it is to say so.
value.literal: Ah—!

value.zh: 注[一]尚書大傳曰「古者諸侯之於天子，三年一貢士。
value.en: Note one: "the Shangshu dazhuan says regional lords presented one candidate every three years.
value.literal: Note [1] The Great Tradition on the Documents says: "In antiquity the feudal lords toward the Son of Heaven, once in three years presented one scholar.

value.zh: 一適謂之好德，再適謂之賢賢，三適謂之有功。
value.en: The first acceptable tribute was 'loves virtue,' the second 'honors worthies,' the third 'has merit.'
value.literal: One meeting was called 'loving virtue,' a second meeting 'honoring the worthy,' a third meeting 'having merit.'

value.zh: 有功者，天子賜以車服弓矢，號曰命。
value.en: Meritorious lords received chariot dress, bow and arrows, and a formal mandate.
value.literal: Those with merit—the Son of Heaven bestowed chariot robes, bows and arrows, and called it a mandate.
